skill.name: ai-image-generation
skill.description: Generate and edit AI images through the inference.sh belt CLI using models such as GPT-Image-2, FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Seedream, Reve, and Topaz. Supports text-to-image, image editing, upscaling, stitching, and model discovery workflows.
skill.summary: Use inference.sh belt commands to generate, edit, upscale, and stitch AI images across multiple model providers.
skill.author: skills-shell

security_audit.summary: The static Ruby backtick and hardcoded URL findings are mostly Markdown false positives, and I found no hidden executable code in SKILL.md. The remaining concerns are contextual: broad belt CLI permission, unpinned remote skill installation guidance, and user content being sent to external image services.

remediation.suggestion: Restrict allowed tools to the specific belt commands required for image generation, or require confirmation before each belt command.
Pin skill and CLI installation instructions to reviewed refs, checksums, or package versions.
Warn users before sending prompts or image URLs to inference.sh or provider apps, and advise against sensitive content.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Belt CLI Permission Surface
semantic_findings.description: The frontmatter permits Bash(belt *), so the assistant may invoke any belt subcommand. This is broader than the documented image workflow and can allow unintended account, file, or network operations through the CLI.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The broad tool permission is explicit in the skill frontmatter. The exact impact depends on the installed belt CLI subcommands, so the confidence is high but not critical.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Remote Skill Installation Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends npx skills add for belt-sh/cli and several inference-sh/skills entries without pinning reviewed versions. Users who follow it may install remote skill content that changes after review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The install guidance is directly visible in the cited lines and uses remote skill identifiers without versions. This creates a clear supply-chain concern, even though it is user-facing documentation.

semantic_findings.title: External Image Service Data Disclosure
semantic_findings.description: The examples send prompts and image URLs to external model apps through belt, but the skill does not place a privacy warning next to those workflows. This can expose sensitive prompts or images if users provide them.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples clearly invoke external image model apps with prompts and image URLs. The finding is limited to disclosure because the external service use is the stated purpose of the skill.

content.value_statement: Image teams often compare many generators, prompts, and edit tools. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code guided belt workflows for image creation and refinement.
actual_capabilities: Guides text-to-image generation with GPT-Image-2, FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Seedream, and Reve app IDs.
Shows image editing flows that send a prompt and source image URL to GPT-Image-2.
Provides upscaling guidance through the Topaz image upscaler app.
Shows how to stitch multiple image URLs into a horizontal or vertical composite.
Directs users to browse available image apps through the belt app store.
limitations: Requires the external inference.sh belt CLI and an authenticated account.
Sends prompts and image URLs to external inference services selected by the user.
Does not include pricing, quota, licensing, or provider policy details.
Does not verify legal rights, consent, or safety of generated images.

use_cases.title: Create Product Mockups
use_cases.description: Generate studio-style product images and refine backgrounds before a campaign review.

use_cases.title: Explore Concept Art
use_cases.description: Compare model choices for characters, environments, posters, and illustration styles.

use_cases.title: Prepare Image Assets
use_cases.description: Upscale, edit, or stitch image URLs for documentation, presentations, and social posts.

prompt_templates.title: Generate A First Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-image-generation to create a product image of a matte black water bottle on a white studio background. Choose a suitable model and explain the next step.

prompt_templates.title: Choose A Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-image-generation to compare GPT-Image-2, FLUX, Gemini, and Seedream for a detailed poster with readable text. Recommend one model and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Edit An Existing Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-image-generation to change the background of this image URL to a warm office scene. Keep the product unchanged and mention any privacy considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Campaign Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-image-generation to plan a workflow for three social ads. Include model choice, prompt direction, editing, upscaling, and final asset review.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a studio image of sneakers for a product page.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a product-focused model, frames a concise prompt, and describes a belt run that returns an image file or hosted result.

output_examples.input: A user provides an image URL and asks for a sunset beach background.
output_examples.output: The skill selects an editing model, keeps the main subject unchanged, and reminds the user that the source image is sent externally.

output_examples.input: A user has two generated images and wants one banner.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests the stitch images app, asks for the image URLs, and describes a horizontal composition workflow.

best_practices: Confirm that prompts and image URLs do not contain confidential or sensitive material.
Choose the model based on output goal, such as text rendering, cost, editing, or resolution.
Record prompts, model names, and settings so successful results can be reproduced.
anti_patterns: Do not send private customer images or unreleased product photos without approval.
Do not assume every model supports editing, LoRA, upscaling, or exact text rendering.
Do not install related skills or CLI tools from unpinned sources in restricted environments.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides an AI assistant to use the external inference.sh belt CLI and supported model apps.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Do I need an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The quick start requires the belt CLI and login before generation.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show image editing with a prompt and a source image URL.

faq.question: Can it upscale images?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes a Topaz image upscaler example through belt.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive images?
faq.answer: Use caution. Prompts and image URLs are sent to external inference services selected in the workflow.
